$comment: Rule catalog — proof assistants and machine certification. Standard 16, and the four never-equate rules of its R1.

rules.title: Proof-assistant sources are accounted for in the ledger
rules.description: Where .lean, .v, or .thy sources exist, at least one claim declares a Formal block referring to them, and the project declares the formal regime in its policy.
rules.rationale: A development nobody's ledger mentions is a formalisation whose relationship to the project's claims is unrecorded, which is the formalisation gap of Standard 16 R4 at its widest.
rules.remediation: Add a Formal block to the claims the development formalises, or declare the sources as work in progress not yet supporting any claim.
rules.$assuranceNote: Observes that formal sources exist and that some claim mentions them. It does not check that every declaration in the development is accounted for.

rules.title: Formal claims record their trusted dependency chain
rules.description: A claim at FORMALIZED_THEOREM or MACHINE_CHECKED_PROOF carries a Formal block naming the assistant and version, the file, the declaration, the axioms, and the pinned external dependencies.
rules.rationale: A reader entitled to know what a machine-checked claim rests on cannot find out any other way. The difference between Lean's standard three axioms and a fourth the project added itself is the difference between a formalisation and a proof under a private assumption.
rules.remediation: Complete the Formal block per Standard 16 R2, including the output of `#print axioms` or `Print Assumptions` as a committed artifact.
rules.$assuranceNote: Checks that the fields are present and non-empty. It does not run the assistant, so it cannot verify that the recorded axiom list is the real one.

rules.title: Project axioms are disclosed
rules.description: An axiom declaration in a project proof-assistant source is listed in the axioms line of some claim's Formal block.
rules.rationale: An undisclosed axiom is a hidden assumption with a compiler's blessing on it: the development builds, the theorem checks, and it is a theorem about a system nobody outside the project accepts.
rules.remediation: List the axiom in the Formal block of every claim whose proof depends on it, or eliminate it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Scans comment- and string-stripped project sources for axiom declarations. It does not see axioms introduced by imported libraries, and it does not compute which declarations actually depend on a given axiom — only the assistant can do that.

rules.title: Formalization gaps are inventoried
rules.description: Every claim carries a Formal field that is either a complete block or the token none, so the set of unformalised claims is explicit.
rules.rationale: Without the inventory, 'we have a Lean development' reads as 'the results are machine-checked'.
rules.remediation: Set the Formal field on every claim. `none` is the honest value for most of them in most projects.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes which claims declare formal status. The gap that matters most — whether the formal statement is the informal one, or an adjacent statement produced by modelling choices — is invisible here and is formal.statement-overclaim.

rules.title: Proof placeholders are tracked
rules.description: Placeholder tokens — sorry, admit, Admitted, oops — present in project proof-assistant sources are reported per file.
rules.rationale: Their presence is not a violation. A formalisation in progress is supposed to have them, and a standard that punished them would push projects to delete the markers rather than the gaps. Reporting them is information.
rules.remediation: None required. Use the report to track what remains, and ensure no claim at machine-checked rank cites a file that appears here.
rules.$assuranceNote: A token scan on comment- and string-stripped sources, so a comment reading 'remove the sorry' does not fire. It does not run the assistant and cannot see placeholders reached through dependencies the repository does not contain.

rules.title: Machine verification is never claimed over a placeholder
rules.description: A claim at FORMALIZED_THEOREM or MACHINE_CHECKED_PROOF cites a formal artifact that contains a placeholder token, cites no formal artifact, or cites a file that does not exist.
rules.rationale: Four different things produce roughly the same green output at a glance — a file that parses, a file that compiles, a helper theorem that checks, and the target proved unconditionally — and only the last is what anyone means by machine-checked.
rules.remediation: Remove the placeholder, or lower the claim to FORMALIZED_THEOREM, which honestly describes a development that builds with gaps remaining.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a cited artifact contains a placeholder token, or that none is cited. It does NOT trace the dependency graph, so a clean pass is not certification — that requires running the assistant and committing the output of `#print axioms` or `Print Assumptions`. A .v file is treated as Coq only when it also contains Coq structure, because .v is equally a Verilog extension.

rules.title: Parsing is never equated with proving
rules.description: A syntactically valid proof-assistant file is reported as establishing a theorem.
rules.rationale: A file that parses has been read by the front end. Nothing has been checked.
rules.remediation: Report the assistant's actual result, and record the claim at the rank that result supports.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector: this is a claim about what someone said, not about the repository's contents. Established by review of the project's own reporting.

rules.title: Compilation is never equated with proving the intended theorem
rules.description: A development that builds is reported as proving the intended theorem, without establishing that the formal statement is the intended one.
rules.rationale: Everything checks and the formal statement is not the theorem the paper claims — a quantifier moved, a hypothesis added, a special case formalised. This is the subtlest of the four and the least detectable, because the artifact is entirely correct.
rules.remediation: State the formal statement alongside the informal one and have a reviewer confirm they agree; record the confirmation as an attestation.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Comparing a formal statement against an informal one is a question about the relationship between mathematics and its encoding, and nothing in the repository could answer it.

rules.title: Proving a helper is never equated with proving the target
rules.description: A checked auxiliary lemma is reported as establishing the target theorem, which remains unproved or placeholder-backed.
rules.rationale: Twelve lemmas check; the main theorem is sorry. The development looks healthy and the target is untouched.
rules.remediation: Name the specific declaration in the Formal block, per Standard 16 R5. 'It is in the development' is not a status.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector for the reporting itself; formal.placeholder-in-chain catches the structural case where the target's cited artifact bears a placeholder.

rules.title: A formal theorem never proves more than its statement
rules.description: A machine-checked declaration is described as establishing a stronger, more general, or differently quantified statement than the one it formalises.
rules.rationale: Formalisation carries enormous authority, and it attaches to the formal statement only. Every formalisation makes modelling choices, and a mismatch means the machine checked something adjacent to the claim.
rules.remediation: Quote the formal statement verbatim beside the informal claim, and record any gap between them as an open obligation.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector, and no prospect of one. Established by a reviewer who reads both the formal statement and the claim.

rules.title: Constructs that enlarge the trusted base are recorded
rules.description: Uses of native_decide, extern bindings, extraction, or code generation are reported so that the trusted base is visible.
rules.rationale: These are legitimate tools and their use is not prohibited. What is required is that a reader can see that the proof rests on more than the kernel.
rules.remediation: None required. Record the construct in the Formal block's dependencies so the trusted base is documented.
rules.$assuranceNote: Names known trusted-base-enlarging constructs found in project sources. It cannot enumerate the actual trusted base, which includes the kernel and every imported library.
